_doc: The cheapest meaningful FIRST test for each application that has none. Authored — this half is a judgement and cannot be derived. The countable half (how many shell testers, how many JVM unit source files, whether the ship workflow executes either) IS derived, by cloud-android-ship-repo-workflow-engine.sh, which merges the two into 1_cicd/dist/data/test-coverage.json on every `./build.sh workflow`. So the counts here can never drift from the tree: `generated files are up to date` regenerates and compares on every push.
_doc_why: 24 of the 28 ship workflows executed no test of any kind, so for 24 applications the pipeline's only question was 'did Gradle exit 0'. An application with zero testers and one with fifty passing testers produced indistinguishable green ticks, and that indistinguishability is the lie — it is why a feature can be marked done, shipped, and be absent from the phone. Writing 24 test suites is a quarter's work, not a task; naming the gap per application, in data, is what makes the debt legible and orderable.
_doc_first_test: Each note names ONE assertion that needs no emulator, no device and no network — a static check over this application's own source, runnable by cloud-android-test-engine.sh's `shell` phase in seconds. Own source only: a first test that reads another application's tree is downgraded to a warning by the foreign-source rule and can never fail a release.

apps.aa_cloud-superapp: Has 52 shell testers. tests.unit.enabled=false, so its step named 'JVM unit tests (fatal on failure)' executes nothing and goes green — its own task, not this one.
apps.ac_cloud-mail: Has 11 shell testers and 755 JVM unit test classes, both executed. The only application in the fleet whose ship run proves anything beyond compilation.
apps.ac_cloud-writer: Has 4 shell testers, executed. Two prove the routing and the absence of a credential; two prove the four configuration pages exist AND are backed by this app's own store, which is the assertion task 209 lacked.
apps.ac_cloud-me: HAD one tester that no workflow ever called. Now executed, plus a second: the release contract (release.variants[].gh_asset / gh_release.asset_name / phone_install.asset_name / artifact.debug) must name ONE file, or the ship publishes an asset the phone never downloads and every run stays green.
apps.ac_cloud-matrix: 836 JVM unit test classes have never executed. Declare tests.unit.task and let them run — by far the largest untouched suite in the repository, and it needs no new assertion written.
apps.ac_cloud-vault: 634 JVM unit test classes have never executed. Same: declare tests.unit.task.
apps.ac_cloud-media-center: 19 JVM unit test classes have never executed. Declare tests.unit.task.
apps.ac_cloud-nix-on-droid: 21 JVM unit test classes have never executed. Declare tests.unit.task.
apps.ac_cloud-termux: 21 JVM unit test classes have never executed. Declare tests.unit.task.
apps.ac_cloud-dialer: 5 JVM unit test classes have never executed. Declare tests.unit.task.
apps.ac_cloud-browser: WebView app: assert every URL its build.json ui declares is absolute and https, so a relative or http entry cannot ship a page the phone renders blank.
apps.ac_cloud-calendar: Five-tab WebView shell: assert every tab id in build.json::ui has a data file and every data file a tab — the same page/data drift ac_cloud-me's tester catches.
apps.ac_cloud-news: WebView over topic feeds: assert every topic declared in build.json has a feed URL and no two topics share an id.
apps.ac_cloud-contacts: Assert every channel type a person entry can declare is one the UI knows how to render — an unknown type is a silently blank row.
apps.ac_cloud-wallet: Assert every wallet record type under data/ parses and carries the fields the card renderer requires.
apps.ac_cloud-nav: Assert the Google/OSM module split in settings.gradle matches build.json::modules — a module in one and not the other builds an APK missing a map provider.
apps.ac_cloud-camera: Minimal fork of GrapheneOS Camera: assert the patch series applies to the pinned upstream revision, so a silent patch-drop cannot ship an unpatched build.
apps.ac_cloud-ide: Three-app constellation: assert each of the three declares a distinct applicationId and gh_asset, so one fork cannot overwrite another's release asset.
apps.ac_cloud-chat: Fork app: assert build.json::forks.chat's pin and patch list match what materialize-fork resolves, so a moved pin cannot ship unnoticed.
apps.ac_c3-morpheus: WebView panel app: assert every panel endpoint in build.json is a mesh 10.0.0.x address — a public hostname is Authelia-gated and renders a login page on the phone.
apps.ac_c3-watchdog: Same shape as c3-morpheus: assert the dashboard endpoint is a mesh address and the WebView is not pointed at localhost, which inside the app means the phone.
apps.ac_cloud-sheets: STALE UNTIL 2026-09-11, and worth saying why: this read 'assert upstream.sha256 is 64 hex characters and source_identity.mode is pin', naming two keys 05b0c6c15 deliberately DELETED when the app stopped being a mirror. Cloud Office is a source build now, and its testers are network-bound by nature — every claim it makes is about a REMOTE object (a pinned Gerrit revision, a pinned upstream APK), so it cannot honestly offer the no-network check the note above asks for. First test: tests/test-configure-flags-exist.sh — every --with-* in upstream.online.configure is a real AC_ARG_WITH at the pinned revision, and the flag upstream actually derives applicationId from is the one we pass, carrying android.application_id. It caught --with-android-package-name, which exists nowhere upstream and which autoconf would have warned about and ignored, shipping the megabuild as org.collabora.app. NOT COVERED: nothing compiles this app, so no tester proves the patch series BUILDS — tests/patches-apply.sh proves only that it applies, and is deliberately not a test-*.sh because it costs a 471 MB fetch.
apps.ab_cloud-libs-shared/lib-apks: Assert the per-asset path sets it derives UNION to the workflow's whole trigger list — publish-gate-blast-radius.test.sh already asserts this; give it a tests block so it runs in the ship job too.
apps.ab_cloud-libs-shared/keyboard-engines: Assert the five bundled modules named in build.json all exist under libs/ — a renamed module currently ships a feature pack missing a feature.
apps.a_solutions/ae-tool_termux-boot: Assert the BOOT_COMPLETED receiver is exported and the host package name it reaches matches ac_cloud-nix-on-droid's applicationId; a mismatch is a boot script that silently never runs.
apps.c_devices/garmin-watchface: Assert every design under faces/ is listed in build.json::build.designs and vice versa — a design not listed is never built and never noticed.
apps.ship-firestack-aar.yml: Not an application: publishes the netstack aar the SuperApp pins. It has no WORK_DIR and no publish gate, so it carries neither the test step nor the published-nothing guard. Its 'Guards on the firestack build contract' step is its only assertion.
